messages:
incident-bot: :warning: INCIDENT detected: continuous-batch performance cliff in us-east-1 (cluster cb-prod-12). Symptoms: queue depth rising, microbatch size oscillation, KV cache eviction spike. Triggered at 2025-09-04T14:00:00Z. Pager: @sophia

sophia: i'm on it. looks like the cb controller rolled a new batching heuristic ~13:58 UTC. seeing huge variance in microbatch sizes and long tail on token generation. attaching quick telemetry snapshot.

sophia: telemetry (p95 latency, error rate, kvcache evict/s):
```
p95_latency: 1800ms (baseline ~120ms)
5xx_rate: 2.6% (baseline ~0.1%)
kvcache_evictions_per_min: 420 (baseline ~16)
queue_length: node-group avg 320 -> growing
active_concurrency: 1600 concurrent requests
```

luca: omg that eviction rate. any recent prefetch tweak or batch size change?

sophia: yes the canary enabled adaptive-prefetch=true + max_microbatch=32 on cb runtime v3.2.1. suspect that prefetch + high concurrency causes cache blowout and increased contention -> microbatch jitter.

dmartin: tagging eng-runtime. @eng-runtime-bot please ack and help triage KV eviction origin and whether we can quickly disable adaptive-prefetch.

eng-runtime-bot: acknowledged. reproducing telemetry. immediate mitigations we can try: 1) disable adaptive-prefetch on canary rollouts 2) reduce max_microbatch to 8 3) apply ingress throttling on affected Routable service to cap concurrency 4) force early cache eviction smoothing.

kai: we should prioritize #2 + #3 as lowest blast radius. disabling prefetch may be higher risk for quality.

sophia: agreed. i'm trying a partial mitigation: scale up cb-proxy replicas by +30% and flip max_microbatch to 8 on the hot nodes. applying now.

sophia: command: 
```bash
# patch runtime config for node-group cb-prod-12
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/runtime/config \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \ 
  -d '{"node_group":"cb-prod-12","max_microbatch":8}'
```

sophia: also pushing temporary ingress throttle for high-volume route /v1/generate: 
```yaml
rate_limit: 1200rps
burst: 2000
policy: reject_overflow
```

luca: any customer impact notes? Slack #support please.

sophia: quick assessment: traffic routing shows elevated latency for customers on us-east-1 multi-tenant pool. Top affected: AlphaFin (premium), BettaChat (self-serve spike), ~12 other small tenants. AlphaFin experiencing >95% requests with >1s additional latency, some 503s on long responses. No data plane errors but timeouts causing retries.

dmartin: starting incident ticket INF-4821 with customers list and mitigation steps. please add any repro logs.

eng-runtime-bot: mitigation applied: max_microbatch=8 on cb-prod-12 (rolled to 60% of nodes) and ingress throttle live. early telemetry after 90s: p95_latency -> 420ms, 5xx -> 0.8%, kvcache_evictions -> 78/min. still above baseline but much improved. continuing to monitor.

sophia: rolling back adaptive-prefetch on remaining nodes now (canary off). command: 
```bash
# disable adaptive prefetch globally while we stabilize
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/featureflags \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \ 
  -d '{"feature":"adaptive-prefetch","enabled":false}'
```

kai: any perf cliff cause analysis yet? my hunch: adaptive-prefetch aggressively warms KV for large prefixes; under high concurrency that heats many shard tags and forces eviction churn because mem working set exceeded. eviction churn -> evict/repopulate -> more prefetch -> positive feedback. microbatch heuristics then see KV miss variance and oscillate batch sizes -> queue blow.

luca: makes sense. for a longer-term fix we should: 1) add backpressure guard on prefetch if eviction rate > X 2) make microbatch adjust more conservatively 3) add a circuit-breaker to drop prefetch for non-critical routes 4) alert on kv_eviction_ratio.

sophia: note for customer comms: AlphaFin SLA might be impacted for 14 minutes during peak. recommend outreach from success team. cc @support.

dmartin: support notified, they will draft templated message.

eng-runtime-bot: small follow-up: we found a config race during rollout where featureflag propagation was partially applied to control-plane caches, leading to mixed heuristics across nodes. ticketed as RUNTIME-2789.

sophia: handing off to night oncall @luca. i've documented steps taken, current telemetry still being polled, rollback of adaptive-prefetch at 14:07 UTC. leaving ingress throttle in place until morning.

luca: taking over. thanks @sophia. i'll keep watch and if p95 > 1s again i'll escalate to infra for emergency scale or consider rolling back cb runtime to v3.2.0.

oncall-shift-bot: :wave: Handoff recorded. Next responder: luca. Handoff notes -> mitigation steps applied: max_microbatch=8; adaptive-prefetch disabled; ingress throttle; scaled proxies +30%. Incident ticket INF-4821 created.

sophia: quick postmortem notes to add later: timeline, root cause (prefetch+high concurrency race -> eviction spiral), mitigations, recommended config limits and rollout gating. also add canary probing that simulates high concurrency bursts.

luca: will follow up in morning with perf graphs and plan for config guardrails. reassign to eng-runtime for longterm fix. good job everyone. :thumbsup:

oncall-shift-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Please update INF-4821 with any lingering customer updates.
